claims.text: MgAl2O4 is an insulating spinel ceramic.
Heat conduction in pristine MgAl2O4 is predominantly phonon-driven, with negligible electronic contributions.
Tailored processing, heat treatments, or compositional modifications can induce and control SRO precipitates in MgAl2O4.
At room or moderately elevated temperatures, phonon–phonon interactions in the proposed ceramic are significant.
Electronic contributions to thermal conductivity remain negligible under the proposed measurement conditions.
SRO precipitates introduce local structural inhomogeneities.
The local structural inhomogeneities associated with SRO precipitates act as scattering centers for propagating phonons.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon scattering times.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon mean free paths.
Reduced phonon mean free paths and scattering times lower lattice thermal conductivity.
MgAl2O4 containing controlled SRO precipitates will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than pristine MgAl2O4 without SRO features.
Time-domain thermoreflectance can quantify the proposed change in lattice thermal conductivity.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity reduction depends on the uniformity, size, and density of the SRO precipitates.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity reduction depends on the processing pathway and resulting microstructure.
